To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the occurrence frequency and intensity of bowel sounds change depending on the type of food, the individual’s health, and their tolerance of the consumed food.

the occurrence frequency and intensity of bowel sounds in the fasting state and after food consumption differ among individuals, and the occurrence frequencies and intensities of bowel sounds in both the fasting state and during food digestion are different for each individual, depending on the type of food.

the occurrence frequency (per unit of time) of bowel sounds in the fasting state and after the consumption of food differs depending on the individual’s constitutional predispositions, health status, and tolerance of foods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the occurrence frequency of minimal intensity bowel sounds in the fasting state and after the consumption of foods.
the development of food evaluation technology that takes the health of an individual and his/her tolerance to the food consumed into account, by investigating changes in bowel sounds.

the evaluation technology for food that is tailored to each individual’s digestive system, and we believe that the method for investigating the changes in bowel activity that we have developed will be useful for the development of foods for patients and for people who require health-care foods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the occurrence frequency per unit of time of bowel sounds of minimal intensity (stethoscopic audible) was higher in the fasting state and lower after eating.

there are differences in the occurrence frequency, duration, and intensity of bowel sounds between the fasting state and the state of digestion, and that there are differences between the occurrence frequency, intensity, and duration of bowel sounds of minimal intensity (audible by amplifier) and those of normal intensity (audible to the human ear) in the fasting and digestion states.
bowel activity in the fasted state and after eating are not synchronized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bowel sounds are a useful index for evaluating the degree of bowel movement, and that our proposed method is useful for the long-term observation of bowel activity in healthy individuals.
bowel sounds are useful in evaluating the degree of bowel movement, especially during digestion, and that the occurrence frequency is a useful index for bowel movement.
bowel activity is affected by the health of an individual, and that bowel activity is not uniform throughout the digestive tract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bowel sounds are useful for evaluating the digestive status of the human body.
bowel sounds can be a useful tool to investigate the digestive system and to develop food evaluation technology that considers the constitutional predisposition of each individual.
bowel activity is affected by the health status of the individual, as well as by the food being consumed.
